source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Capella Operational Management API (REST API surface)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - parallel to the already-promoted capella:data-api concept (Capella Data API / Query Service passthrough); this is the equivalent 'the API surface itself' concept for the management-plane REST API, distinct from Capella's Data API which is a data-plane surface

concepts.label: Capella Management API Key
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - genuinely distinct primitive from capella-role:*/rbac-role:role. It is a credential object that CARRIES one or more Capella roles rather than being a role itself; warrants its own mgmt-api: namespace per this batch's hypothesis

concepts.label: a Capella management-plane role (coarse placeholder)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - coarse placeholder for the object of requiresCapellaRole/assignsRole where this page names 'the appropriate Capella roles' generically rather than a specific role by name. Directly parallel to the existing rbac-role:role data-plane placeholder; needs refinement into capella-role:organization-owner/project-owner/project-data-writer/etc. once a specific role is named (see management-api-start.json, this batch, which names Organization Member specifically)

concepts.label: Free Tier Plan
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - same concept as cloud/billing/upgrade-account.json (existing registry)

relations.subject: mgmt-api:api-key
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the promoted requiresCapellaRole predicate, whose domain_note says its object is normally a specific capella-role:* concept; here the object is the coarse placeholder because the page speaks only generically of 'the appropriate Capella roles'. This directly answers this batch's hypothesis: the Management API does NOT introduce a separate role vocabulary of its own - it reuses the exact same capella-role:* family that gates SQL++ statement execution on Capella (Organization Owner / Project Owner / Project Data Writer), just wrapped in the mgmt-api:api-key credential concept as the thing that carries those roles rather than being checked directly against a user session.
relations.evidence: Couchbase Capella associates API keys with roles and permissions. To access an endpoint, an API key must have the appropriate Capella roles.

relations.subject: capella:management-api
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - same predicate as cloud/indexes/query-without-index.json (5 prior occurrences in the registry); here the whole Management API surface, not just a single feature, is gated by billing-plan tier
relations.evidence: The Couchbase Capella Management API is not available for free tier operational clusters. Upgrade your account to manage deployments with the Management API.

notable_absence.finding: This page never names a specific Capella role (Organization Owner, Project Owner, etc.) for API key access - it only says 'the appropriate Capella roles' and defers to the Management API reference guide per-endpoint. The concrete role names only surface on management-api-start.json (Organization Member) in this batch; the granular per-endpoint role requirements live in the (out-of-scope) Management API reference guide itself, not in this intro page.

cross_component_finding: The Management API's authentication model (mgmt-api:api-key wrapping capella-role:* roles, plus PUT/ETag optimistic concurrency control and audit-by-default) has no equivalent described on any server/ page in the registry - server/'s REST Admin API and cbauth model are not role-scoped by organization/project in the same way. This is a genuinely Capella-only access-control wrapper layered on top of, not replacing, the existing capella-role:* vocabulary.
